# CrossAware

> CrossAware is a personal safety app for pedestrians and cyclists. It automatically lowers media volume (music, podcasts, video, game audio) and plays a short spoken warning when the user approaches a mapped danger zone (danger zones: rail crossings, tram crossings and pedestrian crossings), then restores the volume once they are clear. Danger-zone detection runs on-device; no GPS coordinates are sent to CrossAware's servers.

CrossAware is not a family location-tracking replacement for apps like Life360. It is designed to complement location-sharing apps by adding automatic audio safety that location sharing alone does not provide.

Company: SIA "DAGAR", Riga, Latvia.
Related product: Pause & Pass (https://pauseandpass.com), a separate audio-safety plugin for scooter- and bike-share operators, made by the same company, SIA "DAGAR". Both use the same Riga danger-zone map built from OpenStreetMap. CrossAware users' data is not used in Pause & Pass.
Contact: hello@crossaware.com
Programme: participant in Urban Mobility Incubator 2026 (https://www.urbanmobility.io), supported by EIT Urban Mobility, an initiative of the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT); partners include VEFRESH and the City of Riga.

## Key facts
- Status: Android beta, currently with testers. Not yet public on Google Play. iOS is planned; no iOS version exists yet.
- What it controls: media audio only (music, podcasts, audiobooks, video, game audio). It does not control phone calls, video calls or meeting apps, and it does not mute the microphone.
- Planned (not available): lowering call volume near danger zones.
- Core mechanism: Android geofencing; about 15 metres before a danger zone, media volume is lowered to about 20% (not paused) and a short spoken warning plays: "Uzmanību!" if the device language is Latvian and a Latvian text-to-speech voice is installed, otherwise "Be aware!" in English; volume is restored on exit. Alerts are suppressed at vehicle speed.
- Planned (not available): features for parents, hazard reporting from the app, more cities. No dates.
- Coverage: Riga, Latvia. Danger zones (railway crossings, tram crossings and stops, pedestrian crossings, dangerous intersections) are based on OpenStreetMap data.
- Pricing: free during beta. Paid plans are not yet available.
- Data privacy: continuous location is processed on-device only. The server stores only zone entry/exit events, without coordinates, and deletes them after 90 days.
